PR #5412 closes #5313 in substance. What should happen to it?",
      "options": [
        "A — PM closes #5313 as completed by PR #5412 once merged; leave the PR's Fixes line naming only #5406",
        "B — add 'Fixes #5313' to the PR body so the merge closes both automatically",
        "C — leave #5313 open for a separate follow-up"
      ],
      "recommendation": "A. I deliberately used no closing keyword on #5313 in the PR body: it is a card I was not dispatched and did not claim, and under the shared GitHub identity a state change I make on it is indistinguishable from anyone else's. B would work mechanically but takes a disposition decision that is yours. C is wrong — the PR leaves nothing of #5313 undone; I also answered the one question it explicitly left untested (a bare run in one of the 11 does NOT collect console's 22 foreign files: their configs have no `projects` array, so vitest falls back to the default include relative to the package root and collects the package's own suite — worse than #3378's shape, because the count and the filenames both look right)."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "NOT filed as a new card, deliberately — recorded as a comment on the existing #3240 (open, pm:queue), which already owns exactly this question ('哪些包真的需要本地配置'): the 11 standalone configs are one pre-monorepo template copied eleven times, byte-identical apart from an unused `import path from 'path'` in 7 of them, and what they diverge on is the alias table. Per the card's instruction I established the divergence and did not touch it. Two facts the comment adds for whoever picks #3240 up: its title's '17' is stale (18 non-root configs today, 11 of them divergent), and after PR #5412 those 11 configs are unreachable by any ACCEPTED invocation — CI runs from the repo root, the root config's projects array names only apps/console, and every package-cwd run is now refused — so they are inert configuration that still reads as live. That sharpens #3240 rather than pre-empting it. Comment: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/3240#issuecomment-5357879574",
    "No new issue filed for the 7 unused `import path from 'path'` eslint warnings in the standalone configs — they predate this PR, are warnings not errors, and fall inside #3240's scope (those files' fate); folded into the comment above rather than split into a card of its own.",
    "Noted, not filed: the new repoRootFrom uses `import.meta.url`, not `__dirname`, so this PR adds nothing to the `__dirname`-in-vite/vitest-configs debt tracked in #3592 (pm:on-hold)."
  ]
}

## ACCEPT — PR #5412 enqueued

`repo:objectui` execution seat, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. Marked ready, then auto-merge (SQUASH). All **21** check runs completed: **19 `success`**, 2 `skipped`. Shards 7m26s–9m07s, Type Check 5m38s, Lint 3m53s.

### ⚠️ This card's numbers were wrong and the dev was right to refuse them

The card said 17 packages were uncovered and named `packages/core`, `packages/components`, `plugin-grid`. Measured — by the dev, and independently by me on `origin/main` before writing this:

| | |
|---|---|
| config files, total | **20** (root + 19) |
| import the root config → **covered** (importing executes its module scope) | **8** |
| **standalone → the actual hole** | **11** |

`packages/core/vitest.config.ts` is two lines re-exporting the root config; `packages/components` merges into it. **Both were already refused before any change.** Only `plugin-grid` of the three was genuinely uncovered. "17" was the count of *all* `packages/*` configs, which I garbled into "uncovered" and then repeated in dispatch orders all session. Corrected at the source in the seat post, and on #5403 which inherited it.

⛔ **#5313 recorded this a day earlier with the correct figure of 11**, the same `plugin-grid` measurement, and prescribed exactly the fix taken here. This card is my duplicate of it — I filed the five ruled cards straight from #5393 without a duplicate search, the second time today I broke a rule I put in every dispatch order. Disposition recorded on #5313: it is the original and the more accurate card, so it will be closed as **completed** pointing at PR #5412, ⛔ not marked a duplicate of mine.

### The near-miss worth keeping

The enforcement test's first classifier spelling was `text.includes('vitest.config.mts')` — and **all 11 standalone configs name the root file in the comment explaining why they do not import it**. Every one classified as covered, and the check went **vacuously green over exactly the configs it exists to catch**. It was caught only because two liveness assertions went red. It now matches the import specifier, and that distinction is pinned as its own assertion.

That is the same defect class as the bug being fixed — a coverage claim that reads true and is false — reproduced inside the fix for it, and caught by the liveness pins rather than by luck.

### Verification

- **Reverse verification with a genuine unknown**: `plugin-grid` accepted before / refused after; `packages/core` refused in both; `packages/app-shell` **predicted unknown**, because whether vitest walks upward for a config had to be measured rather than assumed. All three matched, including the unknown. Full sweep: **before 10 refused / 11 accepted → after 21 refused / 0 accepted**.
- The before-state is the false green in its exact shape: package-cwd run in `plugin-grid`, `Test Files 1 passed`, exit 0, **no guard output at all**.
- **Ablation** on the new enforcement test (delete one guard call → red naming that file, 1 failed / 29 passed), restored to 30/30.
- `repoRootFrom(import.meta.url)` replaces eleven hand-counted `../..` literals — a wrong count resolves to a *real* directory, so the guard would keep issuing verdicts against the wrong root, silently. A landmark search either finds the root or throws.
- **Nothing exempted**: CI runs `pnpm test` from the repo root only (`ci.yml:435` rejects `turbo run test`), the 11 configs are not loaded by a root run, and the `OBJECTUI_VITEST_GUARD=off` escape hatch still works.
- ⛔ `.github/workflows/ci.yml` untouched — verified; #5403 owns it and is now in flight.

Three doc surfaces that each claimed the guard lives "in `vitest.config.mts`" were corrected — it is now one of twelve call sites, and stating only the root one is the habit that let this hole persist.

Card closes on merge via `Fixes #5406`.
